Strike by Industrial Intermediate Prod Workers Halts Operations at Key Zimbabwe Sites

HARARE – A widespread walkout by workers in Zimbabwe’s Industrial Intermediate Prod sector entered its third day on Monday, bringing operations at several major plants to a standstill and raising concerns about production targets for the current quarter.

The strike began early Saturday, when union representatives announced that talks over wages and working conditions with the Zimbabwe Intermediate Manufacturers Association had broken down. According to the National Union of Intermediate Process Workers, more than 2,800 employees across five facilities—including those operated by ZimInterprod Ltd., Delta Base Manufacturing, and Harare Intermediates Corp.—have joined picket lines.

Sites in Harare, Bulawayo, and Gweru reported full shutdowns as teams of workers refused to cross picket lines. In a statement, ZimInterprod Ltd. confirmed “all core manufacturing activities have been suspended due to the ongoing industrial action.” At Delta Base Manufacturing’s Gweru facility, a security officer told reporters, “Only management and security staff are present. Production lines are silent.”

Union spokesperson Rudo Chikore said, “Our members are committed to achieving fair pay and safer working conditions. We regret the disruption, but the issues have been ignored for too long.” The union is demanding a 22% wage increase and improved shift safety measures. Employers have so far offered 7%, citing “challenging macroeconomic conditions.”

Industry analyst Blessing Mataruse suggested the strike could cost the sector “at least US$1.5 million per day in lost output,” potentially impacting orders and planned upgrades at the affected sites. “If the impasse continues much longer, companies will need to reconsider their short-term production strategies,” Mataruse added.

Representatives of the Zimbabwe Intermediate Manufacturers Association said negotiations remain open, but no new talks have been scheduled. “We recognize the importance of our workforce and hope to reach a mutually beneficial agreement,” the association said in a statement.

As the strike continues, assembly lines remain idle and workers continue to protest outside plant gates, with no clear resolution in sight.
